Subject: Renewal: EU data residency requirement + APAC pilot

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you’re well — our team at EuroClinics is starting renewal discussions for our Redwood contract (current term ends 2027-01-31). Two items are priorities for us this cycle:

1) EU data residency for all patient PII and logs — needs to be enforceable in contract and in practice (we'd prefer a private deployment or dedicated EU tenancy).
2) APAC pilot — we want a small pilot in Singapore to support three hospitals in Q1; that pilot will validate cross-region failover and burst capacity.

I attached our capacity forecast for Q4 which shows a 2.5x token growth in clinical summarization for the pilot population. Can you send an amended SOW and ballpark pricing for: (a) 24-month renewal with EU residency addendum, and (b) a 6-week APAC pilot with dedicated burst capacity and a cross-region failover SLA?

Please loop in anyone who needs to weigh in (legal/infra). Wei Zhang in APAC is copied here.

Thanks,
Hélène

Hi Hélène / Wei — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. We can support both items but will need to align on a small set of contract changes and an engineering rollout plan. High-level proposal attached: EPM_Renewal_Addendum_v1.pdf and SOW_APAC_Pilot_v1.xlsx.

Summary:
- Term and pricing: recommend a 24-month renewal with a reserved capacity uplift (approx +40% committed GPUs) for the pilot + production runway. We included two pricing tiers in the addendum (pilot-only vs pilot+dedicated pool).
- EU data residency: offer Private (VPC) control plane with EU-dedicated serving capacity—this will keep PII and logs within EU regions. Contract language suggested in section 2 of the addendum.
- APAC pilot & failover: pilot scoped to Singapore region with burst capacity and a cross-region failover policy. Failover will use smart routing to fallback to a hot standby in APAC; we propose a canary test phase before full failover enablement.
- Timeline: proposed kickoff mid-December, pilot go-live target 2027-01-15.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) target pilot capacity from the forecast (tokens/sec), (b) any minimum data-retention limits we must respect, and (c) whether you need Redwood to manage the KMS keys or if you'll supply them?

I'll loop in infra and legal internally to get final pricing and add the specific residency clause.

Best,

Steph / team — I reviewed the SOW and the forecast. Short answers:

- Feasibility: yes. We can provision a EU-dedicated serving pool (Private deployment with EU-region-only nodes) and a Singapore pilot pool. The model variants for the clinical summarization workload fit well with our quantized 8-bit runtime; estimated throughput: ~1.8x tokens/sec compared to baseline with no significant latency impact.
- Failover approach: suggest a staged design — (1) prefix-level KV caching to minimize cold-start cost, (2) smart routing + canary failover for the first 7 days of pilot, (3) automated fallback to APAC standby only if EU capacity is saturated or whole-region outage detected. We should capture max acceptable RTO/RPO in the SLA.
- Risks & timeline: dependency is KMS availability (customer-managed keys require earlier handoff) and on-site network peering for low-latency burst. If we start provisioning resources in early Dec, Jan 15 pilot go-live is achievable but tight.

I attached our SOC2 extract for the residency playbook: SOC2_Report_Q3_2026.pdf — pass this to the customer's security team.

Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Hi Hélène / Wei — following up with the updated addendum and a short summary of agreed items. I’ve attached the formal addendum and the SOW for the APAC pilot. Links: DocuSign (embedded) and HubSpot deal are below.

Key points in the attached addendum (EPM_Renewal_Addendum_v1.pdf):
- Term: 24 months (start 2027-02-01) with early pilot credit applied to first 6 weeks.
- Capacity: +40% reserved capacity for pilot, with optional scale-to-commit tiers defined in section 3.
- Data residency: private EU serving pool. Logs and PII stored in EU region; audit logs accessible per contract with a defined retention window (default 90 days, configurable).
- Failover: canary-based cross-region failover with RTO target 5 minutes for failover to APAC standby. Failover will not replicate EU PII to APAC unless explicit written consent (we added consent language).
- Pricing: included two line items for pilot and production; we offered a 7% multi-region renewal discount when they sign both pilot and 24-month commit (applies to committed monthly base rate).

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the fast turnaround and for capturing most of our asks. Two quick items before we sign:

1) Data retention: can you change the default audit log retention to 30 days (we’ll arrange longer retention via a paid add-on if needed). Please update section 2.3 in the addendum.
2) Clause about PII replication: we need explicit confirmation that we will not replicate any EU patient PII to APAC except for ephemeral copies used by failover during an active outage, and that those ephemeral copies are automatically purged within 24 hours after failover. Update needed in the failover paragraph.

If you can produce a one-line redline or revised addendum with those two tweaks, we’ll sign the DocuSign and target the Jan 15 pilot go-live. Wei will coordinate local peering and KMS handoff.

Regards,
Hélène
